ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Colombian AML/CFT and UBO regime: Ley 526 de 1999 (creation of the UIAF, Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero); Ley 599 de 2000 (Código Penal, arts. 323 et seq. criminalizing money laundering and financing of terrorism); Ley 1121 de 2006; Ley 1453 de 2011 and Ley 1474 de 2011 (security and anti-corruption amendments); Ley 1762 de 2015 (AML and illicit-trafficking instruments); Ley 2010 de 2019 (mandatory final beneficial owner disclosure framework); UIAF Resolución No. 000070 de 2020, as amended (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, RUBF); Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular Externa No. 004 de 2019 and Circular Externa No. 011 de 2021 (SAGRILAFT compliance); and the DIAN tax-beneficiary reporting regime. The framework is aligned with FATF and GAFILAT recommendations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence and good standing of the non-resident corporate shareholder, with sworn Spanish translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., applicable Secretary of State or Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Apostille Convention origin jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney (poder especial) authorizing the Colombian agent and legal representative to execute the S.A.S. incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin or Colombian notary upon acknowledgment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of passports and current tax identification documents of every final beneficial owner, director and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-country notary or Colombian notary for signature authentication
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization if executed abroad in a non-Apostille jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO disclosure declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) prepared for the UIAF Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, together with the SAGRILAFT manual acknowledgment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative of the S.A.S. before a Colombian notary; electronic filing through the UIAF RUBF platform
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; domestic document; no apostille required; UIAF portal submission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory event-driven screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, attorneys-in-fact and material counterparties against: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Sectoral Sanctions lists; UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list and UNSCR 1373 designations; EU consolidated financial sanctions list; UIAF and Superintendencia de Sociedades published Colombian money laundering and terrorist financing risk lists; Procuraduría General de la Nación and Contraloría General registries of persons disqualified from public functions and contracting; and GAFILAT typological sources with adverse-media checks. Politically Exposed Persons require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and verified origin-of-funds documentation under SuperSociedades Circular Externa 004 de 2019 and Circular Externa 011 de 2021. Because the entity anticipates USDC and Stripe payment rails, screening also covers virtual-asset service providers and wallet-address counterparties for sanctions exposure and compliance with Colombian virtual-asset guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES, Registro Único Empresarial y Social (https://www.rues.org.co), operated by Confecámaras in coordination with the Cámara de Comercio of the territorial jurisdiction of the registered domicile, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for Bogotá D.C.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be composed in Spanish and may contain Spanish diacritical marks. The legal suffix S.A.S. or the full form Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada is mandatory. Foreign brand or business names are acceptable only where transliterated or adapted to the Latin/Spanish alphabet, do not mislead as to corporate purpose, do not offend public order or moral standards, and do not create identity or confusion with protected trademarks in the national trademark database. The Cámara de Comercio applies a phonetic and graphic homonymy test against existing registered names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Criptoactivo or Asset Virtual when used in a manner implying regulated financial activity
Colombia when used as a standalone designator that implies official state identity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name homologation, the applicant may: (i) submit a new alternative name application through RUES with a new certificate of availability; (ii) within ten business days of notification, file a recurso de reposición before the issuing Cámara de Comercio based on prior trademark registrations, homonymy certificates or doctrinal criteria; (iii) in the same act or in the alternative, file recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Sociedades, which supervises commercial registry decisions; and (iv) if administrative remedies are exhausted, challenge the final registry act before the Jurisdicción de lo Contencioso Administrativo. The certificate of name availability expires after thirty calendar days and cannot simply be renewed; a new homologation application is required if the incorporation is not registered within that period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtually managed registered offices are conditionally acceptable. The S.A.S. must maintain a genuine terrestrial Colombian address capable of receiving judicial and administrative service of process; this address is recorded in the matrícula mercantil and in the incorporation deed. P.O. boxes or purely postal locations are rejected. For an AI/LLM API platform with remote foreign ownership, the company may operate digitally from abroad but must preserve in-country substance indicators such as a registered agent, complete accounting and corporate records, SAGRILAFT files, tax filings, and a legal representative addressable in Colombia in order to withstand DIAN and Superintendencia de Sociedades economic substance review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 8% during the first operational year for a standard low-risk technology entity with a registered domestic seat, a local legal representative and a compliant SAGRILAFT program. The probability increases to approximately 15-25% where significant stablecoin or cryptocurrency inflows are detected, where foreign state-owned or PEP-linked capital appears in the UBO chain, or where the company applies registry amendments; in such cases unannounced verification of the registered seat and corporate records is a regular supervisory event.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the S.A.S. minuta de constitución and by-laws compliant with Ley 1258 de 2008
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Colombian corporate counsel engaged by the shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard low-risk S.A.S. incorporation, USD 700-1,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaría Pública in the chosen domicile city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Deontological notarial tariff, approximately COP 100,000 to 150,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff scaled to stated capital; minimum tariff approximately COP 140,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 20-30 per month for registered address service

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015 (registration and commercial supervision)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered office; coordinated through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución, or Escritura Pública when capital contributions include assets valued above the statutory threshold
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital may be zero or paid in installments up to two years; cash contributions do not require an escrow account, but foreign investment must be exchanged and registered with Banco de la República under Circular Reglamentaría DCIN 83 when applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF SOCIEDAD POR ACCIONES SIMPLIFICADA. The shareholders, having subscribed the entire share capital, unanimously resolve: (1) To incorporate the company under Law 1258 of 2008, approving its bylaws and share issuance. (2) To adopt the registered office stated in the bylaws. (3) To appoint the Legal Representative and Company Secretary, granting them broad powers for administration, tax filing, and registry formalities. (4) To ratify the tax domicile and instruct preparation of the RUT registration. (5) To authorize all necessary steps before the Chamber of Commerce and DIAN, including signing of public or private instruments, and to obtain all applicable municipal operating permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability verification and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio — Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names for the SAS. Verify that none is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or trademark. Upon approval, reserve the chosen name for 30 days pending later registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of shareholder identification documents (cédula or passport)
Tax identification (NIT) of shareholders if previously registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit alternative names; any administrative delay is cured by completing the online form with corrected alternatives and receiving a new reservation certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of incorporation instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution before shareholders or Notaría Pública when public deed is statutorily required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS bylaws, capital structure, share subscription list, corporate purpose covering ISIC 6201 AI and LLM inference services, and governance rules. If contributions in kind exceed the threshold set by law, elevate the act to a public deed before a notary. Otherwise execute a private document, with signatures, fingerprints, and acceptance of the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Certified draft of incorporation document and bylaws
Proof of registered address (rental or ownership agreement)
Bank certificate of paid-in cash contributions if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Returned documents must be corrected and re-executed; notarial corrections are done through a rectification instrument. If the Commercial Registry quashes the filing, new signatures and conformed copies are submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio — Registry of Commercial Establishments (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation instrument, the name reservation certificate, and the RUES single registration form. Pay the registration fee and the Chamber's administrative tariff. The registry will enter the company registration, issue a commercial registration certificate, and enable the company to present third-party invoices.
required_dossiers: Incorporation instrument (private document or public deed)
Proof of payment of registration and notary fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an objection or fails to record, file a corrected rectification within the opposition period and provide the missing certificate or requisite to the Chamber's legalization office; administrative silence triggers a written cure petition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and foreign investment filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) and Banco de la República for foreign capital registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the NIT/RUT, activate the electronic invoicing system, and register the company's tax characteristics with ISIC activity 6201. For non-resident shareholders, file the foreign investment declaration with Banco de la República through a local commercial bank and obtain the foreign exchange registration certificate. Apply for the digital signature to conduct online procedures.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and valid identity of legal representative
Bylaws and first board resolution appointing officers
Foreign investment filing form if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the RUT, file an official correction through the DIAN portal. Foreign exchange registration errors are cured by presenting a rectified form and supporting documentation to the intermediary bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating permit and occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Mayor's Office (Licencia de Funcionamiento) and local planning authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the commercial operating license (Registro de Establecimiento Comercial) at the municipal office for the registered office address. Arrange for fire safety inspection by the local fire department and an occupancy/structural assessment if the office has special loads or changes of use. Submit the documents online or in person and pay the municipal fee.
required_dossiers: Lease or property ownership deed for the registered premises
Fire safety inspection request and building plans
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requests additional structural or fire-safety modifications, remediate the identified deficiencies and provide corrected building or fire-safety certificates; an appeal is available if the permit is formally denied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Mayor's Office — Subsecretaría de Inspección, Vigilancia y Control; special administrative approval not applicable to AI/LLM API platform
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Establecimiento Comercial / Licencia de Funcionamiento

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) in coordination with Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration only — exempt from full EIA due to non-industrial office-based AI/LLM service with limited physical footprint; environmental declaration may be required by local authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Resolution 631 of 2015 for wastewater (residual limits: BOD5 50 mg/L, COD 75 mg/L); server cooling systems must avoid volatile organic compound emissions; all electrical and electronic waste must be handled under Decree 284 of 2018 and disposed through authorized recyclers

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire department (Bomberos), structural load inspection for server rooms or IT equipment, and workplace health and safety clearance per Resolution 0312 of 2019 before full operation

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - National Tax and Customs Administration; online taxpayer portal at https://www.dian.gov.co and DIAN's transactional platform (SIE - Servicios Informáticos Electrónicos)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a Colombian tax identification number (NIT - Número de Identificación Tributaria) by registering with DIAN through the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) procedure. For foreign digital service providers, registration is performed remotely by filing RUT form through an appointed legal representative or attorney-in-fact having local presence, presenting the foreign company's constitutional documents, proof of legal existence, and confirmation of a local fiscal representative. Once registered, the DIAN assigns the NIT and updates RUT to reflect the entity's status as an IVA responsible party. Domestic SAS entities obtain NIT automatically upon incorporation with the local Chamber of Commerce.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a check-the-box system for SAS corporations; an S.A.S. is invariably a separate taxable entity subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Available elections affecting tax status include: (i) the Simplified Taxation Regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación) under Law 2010 of 2019, combining income tax, VAT, and national consumption tax in one return, available to qualifying SMEs with annual gross income below approximately 80,000 UVT (value adjusted annually); (ii) the Holding Company Regime (régimen de sociedades holding) requiring an equity interest threshold and an election to apply the territorial exemption for foreign-source dividends and capital gains; and (iii) treaty-based or transfer-pricing elections. Hybrid mismatch elections must conform to Decree 2420 of 2018 and the OECD hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Agregado) - Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold applies to entities performing taxable supplies in Colombia; any individual or entity carrying out habitual or occasional taxable activities must register as a VAT responsible party (Responsable del IVA) upon obtaining the NIT. For foreign digital service providers, registration becomes compulsory once digital services are supplied to non-business customers located in Colombia, without regard to turnover volume. Small taxpayers may elect the Simplified Taxation Regime (SIMPLE) only when annual gross income does not exceed approximately 80,000 UVT (the UVT is annually updated; 2025 UVT ≈ COP 49,799, threshold ≈ COP 3.98 billion).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Colombia mandates electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) for all VAT-registered taxpayers, including foreign digital service providers, with a real-time clearance model administered by DIAN. Invoices must be transmitted to DIAN's electronic invoicing system before delivery to the buyer, using DIAN's approved web service (API) or a DIAN-certified technology operator. Each invoice must include a unique electronic code (CUFE - Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) with a cryptographic stamp (CUDE for simplified invoicing), a 2D barcode/QR, and DIAN's validation response. Foreign suppliers selling to Colombian non-business consumers may use DIAN's simplified 'factura de venta' and remittance of data in bulk through the designated web portal under Resolution 165 of 2023. Non-compliance triggers exclusion from invoicing systems, monthly fines, and inability to claim export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported services is available under Article 481(e) of the Colombian Tax Statute when: (i) the service is executed entirely within Colombian territory but exclusively for the benefit of users or entities abroad, or is provided to a Colombian user that in turn exports the service; (ii) the recipient of the service has domicile or residence abroad; (iii) the participation of the exporter inside Colombia is not in the provision of services used or consumed economically in Colombia; and (iv) foreign evidence of receipt and cross-border payment is maintained. For exports of computer software, AI/LLM API inference services, and technology platform services, the exporter must also demonstrate that the digital service is supplied via internet, cloud infrastructure, or telecommunications system and that the beneficiary is located outside Colombia at the point of use. The DIAN requires the exporter to have all supporting documentation proving the true export nature and the effective integration of the service into the foreign client's business/use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - DEX or administrative equivalent), where applicable
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill proving international transport for exported goods (for service exports, an electronic service export statement and contract evidence)
Certificate of Foreign Currency Remittance (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas / Formulario No. 4) issued by a Colombian bank showing the repatriation of funds from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN conducts selective export verification within the general five-year statute of limitations. A false or unsupported zero-rating claim triggers the penalty for inexact or incomplete returns under Article 648 of the Tax Statute, equal to 200% of the understated tax, plus default interest (currently above 30% annually). Retroactive clawback converts the export to a taxable transaction, requiring the exporter to remit the 19% VAT on the full invoice value, with interest from the original transaction date. Additional penalties apply for repeated violations, including a fine up to 100% of the tax omitted for not invoicing, and cancellation of the invoice authorization. Where the fraudulent claim is intentional or involves forged documentation, criminal tax evasion sanctions under Articles 477 and 479 of the Colombian Criminal Code may apply, including imprisonment for up to nine years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through the Exchange Office and the Foreign Exchange Regulation Division, together with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for prudential supervision and DIAN for customs- and tax-related foreign transaction enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a free-market, managed-float currency system. Current-account transactions, including service exports such as AI/LLM API platform revenue, are convertible if channeled through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries under the obligation of 'canalización' (mandatory routing through the official FX market). Capital-account inflows are freely convertible but require registration with Banco de la República via an authorized bank. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted without quantitative restriction once the corresponding foreign direct investment has been registered and the dividend distribution satisfies Colombian corporate and tax law; practical hurdles include completing the FDI exchange declaration, evidencing tax residency for treaty relief, timely filing of annual tax returns, and satisfying bank-level source-of-funds inquiries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exports of goods and services, including AI API usage fees, the resulting foreign currency proceeds must be canalized through the Colombian FX market within six (6) months from the date of receipt/collection, as established by Banco de la República's Circular Reglamentaria DCIN 83 and applicable foreign-exchange regulations. There is no mandatory fixed percentage conversion into Colombian pesos; however, the full amount, net of permissible compensation deductions and authorized foreign-operating expenses, must be repatriated into Colombia or deposited into a local foreign-currency account with an authorized bank. Failure to comply can trigger exchange-limit sanctions, tax disallowances, and blocked future FDI/profit remittance registrations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multicurrency USD/COP corporate account and foreign-exchange derivative line
Operational account, foreign currency deposit account, and commercial credit/LC facility
Corporate current account and FX hedging desk for USD/COP covered derivatives
Corporate savings/checking account and capital escrow-aligned operational account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium viability. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer are not authorized Banco de la República foreign-exchange intermediaries and cannot execute compliant Colombian 'canalización' declarations. They may be used as ancillary collection/expense rails but must never be the exclusive settlement path for export-service receipts because they do not produce exchange declarations accepted by banks, tax authorities, or Banco de la República. Cryptocurrency/stablecoin platforms facilitating USDC-derived revenue remain outside the official FX system and require local bank conversion evidence before being recognized as compliant export proceeds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, tier-1 Colombian banks require either the legal representative, a director with sufficient powers, or a locally appointed attorney-in-fact to attend an in-person KYC and risk interview at a Colombian branch before account activation. Fully remote onboarding is not standard for a non-resident-owned S.A.S., especially with digital/AI and cryptocurrency-linked income. A physical presence by the beneficial owner or senior finance director is strongly recommended; the bank may additionally demand notarized powers of attorney, apostilled corporate documents, and certified Spanish translations of foreign entity records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital business model with cross-border AI API revenue and token-based payments (USDC) producing source-of-funds questions beyond a normal low-risk technology score.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed platform service agreements, tax invoices issued, payment processor statements showing USDC-to-fiat conversion, exchange transaction history, wallet due diligence, proof of registration with a crypto-asset service provider authorized in the client's domicile, and an internal AML/KYC manual demonstrating source-of-funds controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or partially undisclosed beneficial-ownership chain involving intermediate foreign entities, making the UBO declaration difficult to complete under Colombian SARLAFT rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Cámara de Comercio certificate, apostilled corporate registry documents for every intermediate foreign company, sworn UBO forms for each natural-person controller, certified Spanish translations, tax residency certificates, notarized ownership chart, and an independent legal opinion confirming no undisclosed control layers exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI to the S.A.S. being flagged for artificially inflated capitalization used to support future dividend remittances or capital-flight scenarios.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capitalization business plan, underlying revenue and operating-expense forecasts, valuation memo for any contributed technology/IP, bank statements proving the source of investor funds, exchange declaration signed by the legal representative, and documentation that operational substance exists in Colombia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party disbursements to an overseas AI technology provider or IP owner being classified as trade-based money-laundering or revenue migration risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany service and licensing agreements in Spanish and English, transfer-pricing documentation, proof of actual API/model usage, royalty calculation models, operational-substance records in Colombia, valid commercial invoices, and bank-confirmed purpose codes matching the declared disbursement reason.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign capital injection must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas investor's bank to the S.A.S.'s operational account held at an authorized Colombian bank. The receiving bank will require and file the 'Declaración de Cambio' using the exchange purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment ('Inversión de capital del exterior'). The wire advice must clearly identify the S.A.S. NIT, the investor entity, and reference the capital-call resolution and the company's RUT. The foreign investment must be registered in Banco de la República's international-investment statistics through the authorized bank within the regulatory filing window; without such registration, future dividend distributions, profit remittances, and return-of-capital execution will be blocked or subject to fines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For foreign vendor and technology payments, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 beneficiary-payment wires and, for larger infrastructure or hardware purchases, irrevocable commercial documentary letters of credit issued by the local tier-1 bank. Local COP payments to Colombian suppliers, payroll, and tax obligations should be routed through ACH Colombia, CENIT, or the low-value payment clearing system operated by the Colombian Central Counterparty infrastructure. All outbound wires must be accompanied by a valid exchange declaration, source-of-funds documentation, and commercial invoices to maintain FX and tax traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on USD/COP with Banco de la República-authorized banks and financial intermediaries
Deliverable USD/COP forward contracts settled through official Colombian FX market channels
Currency swaps between USD and COP for balance-sheet and cash-flow hedging
USD/COP exchange-traded and OTC options used exclusively for bona fide underlying commercial exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched funding or long-term infrastructure obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio competente via the Unified Business Registry platform (RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year, measured by the anniversary of the initial commercial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge plus additional chamber penalties; continued failure triggers loss of registration status, inability to obtain valid commercial certificates, evidentiary restrictions, and administrative strike-off after prolonged non-renewal, ultimately exposing the S.A.S. to dissolution procedures under the Colombian Commercial Code.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Shareholders’ Approval Deposit (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio competente via RUES, following shareholder approval at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within three months after fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a calendar fiscal year); statutory deposit with the Chamber within one month after approval (by 30 April for a calendar fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties imposed by the Chamber of Commerce and Superintendencia de Sociedades; legal representatives may be fined, financial statements lose third-party evidential value, and the S.A.S. may be prevented from lawfully distributing profits until the filing is regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; any change in final beneficial ownership arising from a share transfer must be updated within one month after the transfer is recorded in the shareholders’ register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate RUBF information may trigger DIAN monetary penalties based on UVT values, restriction of tax refunds and certificates of compliance, and additional enforcement measures by tax and corporate authorities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) and corresponding financial audit are compulsory when the S.A.S. exceeds the thresholds of Article 203 of the Colombian Commercial Code, generally total assets of at least 5,000 current monthly minimum wages (SMMLV), gross annual revenue of at least 3,000 SMMLV, more than 200 employees, or when the company is subject to superintendency vigilance; otherwise the S.A.S. may lawfully operate without a Revisor Fiscal unless the shareholders voluntarily appoint one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Normas de Información Financiera (NIF) under Law 1314 of 2009; full IFRS for Group 1 entities, NIF for SMEs for Group 2, and simplified NIF for micro entities; the statements must be prepared in COP and comply with the applicable technical, accounting and financial reporting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 2010 of 2019 and DIAN Resolution 000070 of 2023, the S.A.S. must annually confirm and update the final beneficial owner information in the RUBF between 1 January and 31 March. Any share transfer that changes the final beneficiary or the control chain must be reported within one month after the transfer is registered in the corporate books. The company must also reconcile the RUBF data with the shareholders’ register and keep documentary evidence of the ownership chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $900 – $2,500 for a compact IFRS-compliant financial statements audit; $3,000 – $7,000 if a Revisor Fiscal appointment becomes mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays in Colombia. The Colombian tax system does not grant broad-based CIT exemptions for AI/LLM API platform companies. However, taxpayers may benefit from the deduction of 50% of the equity investment in certain innovative projects approved by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (up to 25% of taxable income for the respective tax year), and a VAT exemption on the import or sale of AI-related software services that qualify as 'software' for export. For the first taxable year of new employment, an additional deduction of 50% of payroll wages for employees under 28 years old may apply if the S.A.S. meets the employment conditions under Article 235-2 E.T. Companies taxed under the general regime are also subject to the surtax for equity (impuesto al patrimonio) only when net equity exceeds COP 0, as this is a normal wealth tax outside the CIT. The effective rate for the AI platform, assuming no special deductions and full taxable profit, approaches the headline 35% plus the municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) and the national consumption tax on certain digital services, with no reduction for foreign shareholders unless treaty relief applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed electronically through the DIAN portal (Muisca / DV to be replaced by the new electronic filing system). Foreign-owned S.A.S. entities must file under the general regime as responsible taxpayers (Régimen Ordinario del Impuesto sobre la Renta).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the deadlines established by the DIAN for the applicable tax year. For tax years ending December 31, the filing deadline ranges from September of the following year, depending on the last two digits of the NIT (Tax ID). Grid: NIT ending 00-01: third business day; 02-03: fourth business day; 04-05: fifth business day; 06-07: sixth business day; 08-09: seventh business day; 10-11: eighth business day; 12-13: ninth business day; 14-15: tenth business day; 16-17: eleventh business day; 18-19: twelfth business day; 20-21: thirteenth business day; 22-23: fourteenth business day; 24-25: fifteenth business day; 26-27: sixteenth business day; 28-29: seventeenth business day; 30-31: eighteenth business day; 32-33: nineteenth business day; 34-35: twentieth business day; 36-37: twenty-first business day; 38-39: twenty-second business day; 40-41: twenty-third business day; 42-43: twenty-fourth business day; 44-45: twenty-fifth business day; 46-47: twenty-sixth business day; 48-49: twenty-seventh business day; 50-51: twenty-eighth business day; 52-53: twenty-ninth business day; 54-55: thirtieth business day; 56-57: thirty-first business day; 58-59: thirty-second business day; 60-61: thirty-third business day; 62-63: thirty-fourth business day; 64-65: thirty-fifth business day; 66-67: thirty-sixth business day; 68-69: thirty-seventh business day; 70-71: thirty-eighth business day; 72-73: thirty-ninth business day; 74-75: fortieth business day; 76-77: forty-first business day; 78-79: forty-second business day; 80-81: forty-third business day; 82-83: forty-fourth business day; 84-85: forty-fifth business day; 86-87: forty-sixth business day; 88-89: forty-seventh business day; 90-91: forty-eighth business day; 92-93: forty-ninth business day; 94-95: fiftieth business day; 96-97: fifty-first business day; 98-99: fifty-second business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT, taxpayer name, and tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the S.A.S. NIT and legal name; the non-resident parent company is not named on the return except in the beneficial owner annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory deductions and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute gross AI/API platform revenue from token usage and fees, less operating expenses, depreciation, amortization, and deductions. Include international revenue sourced in Colombia for services used in the country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 35% CIT rate on taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 35% rate. No reduction is available for the foreign shareholder unless treaty provisions apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for industry and commerce tax paid to the municipality
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ICA paid on AI services can be deducted only when directly related to the income-producing activity and when the return is filed in the corresponding municipality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Minimum taxable income calculated as 0.5% of net equity plus 3% of gross billings in certain cases
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. must ensure taxable income is not less than the presumptive income; this often captures foreign-owned IP companies with low local cost bases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax prepayments and withholdings borne by the company during the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the 2.5% income tax withholding on foreign remittances to the U.S. parent if any payments were made for cross-border services or royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses offset against current-year taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset only losses generated in Colombia and supported by prior filed returns. Losses from the parent company cannot be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8: Net Tax Payable (Saldo a Pagar)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after prepayments and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through the DIAN electronic banking system in Colombian pesos before the statutory deadline. The foreign shareholder has no separate payment obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax due, with a minimum penalty of 10 UVT (Unidad de Valor Tributario). Late payment interest: interest accrues at the current lending rate (mora) from the day after the deadline until payment. Additional fines may apply for inaccuracies: 160% of the understated tax if the return is incorrect or fraudulent, and 20% of the omitted value for not including information required under Article 631 E.T.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% for dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders. Dividends paid out of profits that have already been subject to the 35% CIT are subject to an additional 7.5% withholding when paid to individuals or entities resident abroad. If the distribution exceeds the taxable income calculated by the DIAN, the excess is taxed at the 35% rate and then at 7.5% on the distribution. For the U.S. parent, the 7.5% rate is the final withholding and is the effective tax cost on repatriation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Colombia does not have a comprehensive income tax treaty with the United States. The U.S.-Colombia Tax Treaty (2012) has not entered into force. Therefore, no DTA relief and no reduced dividend withholding rate apply to U.S. residents. For taxpayers resident in treaty jurisdictions (e.g., Canada, Mexico, South Korea, Chile, Spain, Portugal, Switzerland, France, Germany, UK, Netherlands), protocol: (1) Obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (CERT) from the foreign tax authority, authenticated/apostilled and translated into Spanish if required; (2) Submit the certificate to the Colombian withholding agent before the payment date; (3) Complete the DIAN Form 160 or the corresponding information return declaring the beneficial owner; (4) The Colombian withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate at source; (5) If the withholding was made at the statutory rate, the non-resident may file a corrective return before the DIAN to request a refund/compensation, supported by the certificate and proof of payment; (6) Apply the domestic anti-abuse rules and LOB clauses under the relevant treaty. Where no treaty exists, the statutory rate applies without further administrative action.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT rate of 15% (or the 35% rate if the royalty payer is not a responsible taxpayer) for payments to non-residents for the use of software, patents, IP, and technical know-how, unless a treaty reduces the rate (e.g., France, Spain, Switzerland, Korea: 10%; Canada: 10%; Netherlands: 10%; Portugal: 10%; Mexico: 10%; Chile: 10%; UK: 10%). Interest: statutory WHT 15% on interest paid to non-residents; treaty rates may reduce to 10% or 5% depending on the jurisdiction (e.g., Germany: 10%, Canada: 10%, Spain: 10%, Switzerland: 10%, Netherlands: 10%, Chile: 5%, Mexico: 15%, South Korea: 5% for financial institutions). Payments to residents of non-treaty countries remain at the statutory 15% withholding. Additionally, remittances for technical services and consulting are subject to a 15% WHT, but AI API platform fees charged by a foreign parent to the Colombian entity will trigger a 15% WHT (or 35% if not registered as a responsible taxpayer); a service fee remittance to the U.S. parent is subject to 15% WHT on the gross payment unless the parent has a permanent establishment in Colombia, in which case the PE profits are taxed at 35%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File for taxpayers with gross assets exceeding COP 100,000 million (approximately USD 25 million) or gross income exceeding COP 250,000 million (approximately USD 62.5 million), or whose transactions with related parties exceed COP 25,000 million (approximately USD 6.2 million). Additionally, a formal Informe de Precios de Transferencia (Local File) must be filed with the DIAN through the official Transfer Pricing Information Return (Form 120) if the taxpayer individually or jointly with related parties has gross income exceeding COP 50,000 million OR if it conducts transactions with related parties in countries with preferential tax regimes. S.A.S. tech platforms below these thresholds must still file Form 120 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) if they carry out transactions with related parties abroad and their gross income exceeds 15,000 UVT (approx. COP 684 million for 2025) and their wealth exceeds 40,000 UVT (approx. COP 1,826 million for 2025). The full Local File and Master File documentation (Diligencia Documental) must be submitted no later than the transfer pricing return deadline, typically the same day as the income tax return for the respective fiscal year.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price): best for AI API services if external comparable token-pricing can be identified.
Resale Price Method: suitable for distribution activities that embed the AI platform as a reseller.
Cost Plus Method: appropriate where the Colombian S.A.S. performs contract software development for the foreign parent and incurs predictable costs.
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method): preferred for routine AI infrastructure or LLM inference services; use the Berry ratio or operating margin.
Profit Split Method: fits integrated, unique-risk contributions in co-development of LLM models and IP ownership.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply the OECD Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a stand-alone doctrine. However, Colombian anti-abuse rules, including the 'substance-over-form' principle under Article 869 E.T., Piercing of the corporate veil doctrine, and the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) introduced in 2020 in the framework of the OECD BEPS initiative, permit the DIAN to disregard transactions or entities lacking economic substance. The S.A.S. must demonstrate that it has physical offices, employees, and sufficient technical capability to perform AI/LLM infrastructure operations; otherwise, the DIAN can reclassify revenues as directly earned by the foreign parent, denying treaty benefits and imposing 100% penalty on understated tax. The presence of bank accounts, contracts, and routine bookkeeping is insufficient if the company has no local decision-making capacity. Under the S.A.S. law (Law 1258 of 2008), the veil can be pierced when the S.A.S. is used for fraud, tax evasion, or misuse of legal personality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to include AI/API revenue in the tax return, overstating deductions, or using the S.A.S. shell to divert profits to a U.S. parent while maintaining no real operations in Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion sanctions under the Colombian Criminal Code (Law 599 of 2000, Article 400) and Article 647 E.T.: a fine of 160% of the evaded tax, plus imprisonment of 4 to 9 years for individuals who evades taxes in an amount exceeding 100 SMMLV (minimum monthly wages). The S.A.S. is subject to a penalty equal to 160% of the understated tax and interest; tax return nullity can be declared by DIAN.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Use of Shell / Conduit Company (Interposición de sociedad)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating the S.A.S. solely to repatriate AI licensing royalties or API fees through invoices for services that are not actually rendered in Colombia, with no employees, no physical presence, and no business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 869 E.T.: DIAN may ignore the S.A.S. as the taxpayer and attribute the income directly to the U.S. principal, resulting in a 35% CIT assessment on the full income plus a 160% penalty and 25% surcharge for understatement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Crypto Compliance (Riesgo de lavado de activos)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC or other crypto payments without performing customer due diligence (CDD), maintaining anonymous API token sales, or transferring funds to a foreign parent through unregistered crypto wallets without banking records. Although AML risk tier is 'Low_Risk_Standard', URD (Unidad de Riesgo) rules under Law 1121/2006 require financial risk management for non-financial entities that develop activities with digital assets when subject to the UAF (Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero) supervision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Colombian AML framework, non-reporting results in fines up to 1,200 SMMLV and the suspension of commercial operations. If laundering is proven, Article 323 of the Criminal Code imposes imprisonment of 9 to 15 years and fines from 650 to 50,000 SMMLV. Directors who fail to report suspicious transactions can be individually criminally indicted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure (Incumplimiento en precios de transferencia)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not submitting Form 120 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) or omitting the Local File / Master File when the S.A.S. exceeds the 15,000 UVT gross income threshold and carries out cross-border related-party API access fees or cost-sharing arrangements with the foreign AI parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to 5% of the gross value of the non-declared transactions; the DIAN can issue an independent determination using the TNMM/Profit Split method and adjust taxable income upwards by the difference. Failure to submit documentation when required: penalty of 0.5% of the transactional value per month, up to a maximum of 5%; death of the cross-border documentation privilege is not optional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Omission of Withholding Taxes on Cross-Border Remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a foreign parent for model licensing royalties, technical support, or management services without applying the 15% withholding, or distributing dividends without making the 7.5% dividend withholding (if profits are already taxed at 35%) and reporting in the annual withholding return (Form 1738).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The non-withheld sum is due with interest; the penalty equals 100% of the tax not collected. The designated director or legal representative may be jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax; the DIAN may block the NIT and cancel the operating license.
